notes: Edit these banks, then run python3 scripts/build.py. Figures are copied from MoneyBySharma's already-checked sources (cheat sheet and guides), not newly verified for this preview. Set preview to false before any live publish.

tips.title: The ISA allowance is £20,000 this tax year
tips.body: In 2026/27 you can put up to £20,000 into ISAs, split across cash, stocks and shares, Innovative Finance and Lifetime ISAs. Unused allowance does not roll over into next year.
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

tips.title: Savings protection is £120,000, not £85,000
tips.body: The Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) protects eligible deposits up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence. The limit was £85,000 until 30 November 2025. Some brands share a licence, so check if your accounts are with the same bank.
tips.checked: as at 1 December 2025 (on the site cheat sheet)

tips.title: The Personal Allowance is £12,570 – until income is high
tips.body: Most people in England, Wales and Northern Ireland can earn £12,570 in 2026/27 before Income Tax. It is reduced by £1 for every £2 of income over £100,000, and is frozen until April 2031. Scotland has its own bands for non-savings income.

tips.title: An emergency fund is a rule of thumb, not a product
tips.body: MoneyHelper's rule of thumb is three to six months' essential outgoings in an instant-access account, so an unexpected bill does not force you onto a credit card or to sell investments at a bad time. How much is enough depends on your situation.
tips.source: MoneyHelper – Emergency savings: how much is enough?

tips.title: Don't miss your employer's pension contribution
tips.body: If you have a workplace pension, contributing enough to get the full employer contribution is money you would otherwise miss. The legal minimum is 8% of qualifying earnings in total, with at least 3% from the employer. Qualifying earnings are currently £6,240 to £50,270.
tips.source: GOV.UK – Workplace pensions: what you, your employer and the government pay
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

tips.title: Expensive debt usually costs more than savings earn
tips.body: Interest on credit cards and overdrafts is often much higher than the interest you can earn on cash. Clearing expensive debt first is a general principle, not a product recommendation – then think about saving and investing what is left.
tips.checked: general principle used on the site cheat sheet (12–28 October 2026)

tips.title: Bank Rate is 4.00% from 5 November 2026
tips.body: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4.00% on 5 November 2026. It influences what banks may pay on savings and charge on some mortgages, but your own rate is set by your provider. It is worth checking whether that rate beats inflation after tax.

tips.title: The Personal Savings Allowance is not the same for everyone
tips.body: Outside an ISA, you may get a Personal Savings Allowance on interest: £1,000 if you pay basic-rate tax, £500 if you pay higher-rate tax, and £0 if you pay additional-rate tax. Interest inside an ISA is tax-free and does not use up this allowance.
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

tips.title: If someone claims to be your bank, hang up and dial 159
tips.body: Criminals can make a number look genuine. Hang up, wait a moment, and call 159 – or use the number on the back of your card – rather than a number you were given on the call. Do not share passwords, PINs or one-time codes.
tips.source: Stop Scams UK – Get help now

tips.title: Forward scam texts to 7726, and emails to report@phishing.gov.uk
tips.body: You can report suspicious texts by forwarding them, free, to 7726. Suspicious emails can go to report@phishing.gov.uk. To report fraud itself, use Report Fraud on 0300 123 2040 (in Scotland, 101).
tips.source: GOV.UK – Report suspicious emails and texts

tips.title: Section 75 can protect some credit-card purchases
tips.body: If you pay for something that costs more than £100 and up to £30,000, and you pay at least part of it by credit card, the card provider can be jointly liable with the retailer if something goes wrong. This is a legal right under Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act 1974. It does not apply in the same way to debit cards.

tips.title: Online, phone and mail-order buys usually have a 14-day cooling-off period
tips.body: For most goods bought online, by phone or by post you can cancel within 14 days of receiving the item, with no reason needed, and you then have a further 14 days to return it. Some items are excluded. In-store purchases do not automatically have the same right.
tips.source: GOV.UK – Accepting returns and giving refunds

tips.title: Faulty goods have a 30-day short-term right to reject
tips.body: If something you buy is faulty, you have a short-term right to reject it within 30 days and ask for a refund. After that, other rights such as a repair or replacement can still apply. This is separate from changing your mind.

tips.title: The Current Account Switch Service is designed to take 7 working days
tips.body: If both banks are in the Current Account Switch Service, the switch is designed to complete in 7 working days. Payments should be redirected, and there is a guarantee of refunds if the switch goes wrong.
tips.source: Current Account Switch Service – The switching process

tips.title: A Lifetime ISA bonus sits inside the £20,000 ISA allowance
tips.body: You can open a Lifetime ISA aged 18 to 39 and pay in up to £4,000 a year until 50. That £4,000 counts towards the £20,000 ISA allowance, and the government adds a 25% bonus (up to £1,000 a year). Penalty-free withdrawals are tightly limited, mainly a first home costing £450,000 or less, or from age 60.
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12–17 October 2026)

tips.title: The pension annual allowance is £60,000 for most people
tips.body: In 2026/27 the annual allowance for most people is £60,000. It covers all contributions, including your employer's. Tax relief on your own contributions usually applies up to 100% of your UK earnings, or £3,600 gross if you have little or no earnings. Very high incomes can see the allowance tapered.
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

tips.title: The earliest most people can access a private pension is rising
tips.body: The normal minimum pension age is 55, and it rises to 57 on 6 April 2028. Some people have a protected pension age. This is different from State Pension age, which you can check on GOV.UK.

tips.title: The full new State Pension is £241.30 a week this year
tips.body: The full new State Pension is £241.30 a week in 2026/27, about £12,548 a year. You only get the full amount if you have a complete National Insurance record. You can check your record and State Pension age on GOV.UK. A figure for April 2027 has been announced, but that is a future year.
tips.source: GOV.UK – The new State Pension: what you'll get
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

tips.title: The Capital Gains Tax allowance is £3,000
tips.body: In 2026/27 the annual Capital Gains Tax exempt amount is £3,000. Above that, the rates are 18% for basic-rate taxpayers and 24% for higher- and additional-rate taxpayers. Gains inside an ISA or a pension are not subject to UK Capital Gains Tax in the usual way.
tips.source: GOV.UK – Budget 2025 OOTLAR Annex A: rates and allowances
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

tips.title: The dividend allowance is £500
tips.body: In 2026/27 the dividend allowance is £500. Above that, dividend tax rates are 10.75% for basic-rate taxpayers, 35.75% for higher-rate taxpayers and 39.35% for additional-rate taxpayers. Dividends inside an ISA are not taxed.
tips.source: GOV.UK – Budget 2025 OOTLAR Annex A: rates and allowances
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

tips.title: A Junior ISA has its own £9,000 allowance
tips.body: A Junior ISA can be opened for a child under 18, with a £9,000 allowance in 2026/27. That is separate from the adult £20,000 ISA allowance. The money is the child's, and they can normally access it when they turn 18.
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

tips.title: Some people can earn up to £5,000 of interest at 0%
tips.body: On top of the Personal Savings Allowance, a starting rate for savings can give 0% tax on up to £5,000 of interest. It is reduced by £1 for every £1 of other income above the Personal Allowance, so it mainly helps people with modest earned income.
tips.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

tips.title: The Direct Debit Guarantee covers errors, not a change of mind
tips.body: If an organisation or your bank makes a Direct Debit error, the Direct Debit Guarantee says you are entitled to a full and immediate refund. It is not a way to cancel a purchase you simply no longer want. Keep the official wording on any Direct Debit instruction you sign.
tips.source: Direct Debit scheme – Direct Debit Guarantee

tips.title: FSCS investment protection does not cover a fall in value
tips.body: If an authorised investment firm fails, the FSCS can protect eligible investment business up to £85,000 per person, per firm (for failures after 1 April 2019). It does not pay you just because an investment went down in value. Your capital is at risk when you invest.

tips.title: A representative APR is not a promise to everyone accepted
tips.body: A representative APR must be available to at least 51% of people who are accepted. Up to 49% can be offered a higher rate. Always read the actual rate and terms you are offered, not just the advertised figure.

tips.title: Breathing Space can pause most interest for up to 60 days
tips.body: In England and Wales, the Debt Respite Scheme (Breathing Space) can give up to 60 days of legal protection from creditors, with most interest and charges frozen. It is a formal process, not an informal request, and it is worth reading the official guidance or speaking to a free debt adviser.

tips.title: Investing is generally for money you won't need soon
tips.body: A common rule of thumb, used on this site and by MoneyHelper-style guidance, is that money needed within about five years usually belongs in cash, because investment values can fall and stay down for years. Money for the long term has more time to ride out those patches. Investments can fall as well as rise, and you may get back less than you put in.
tips.source: MoneyHelper, and the site guide to cash versus inflation

tips.title: Check whether your savings rate beats inflation after tax
tips.body: The Bank of England's inflation target is 2%. Consumer Prices Index inflation was 3.5% in the year to September 2026 (ONS, published 21 October 2026; next release 18 November 2026). If your savings rate is below inflation after any tax, your money buys a little less over time even if the balance rises.
tips.source: ONS – Consumer price inflation, September 2026; Bank of England inflation target
tips.checked: CPI checked 26 October 2026; Bank Rate 5 November 2026

tips.title: Third-party cover is the legal minimum to drive
tips.body: To drive on UK roads you must have at least third-party motor insurance. That is the legal minimum; it does not cover damage to your own car. Other types of cover exist, but this tip is only about the legal floor, not which policy to buy.

tips.title: You can now pay into more than one ISA of the same type
tips.body: Since 6 April 2024 you can pay into more than one ISA of the same type in a tax year, as long as you stay within the overall £20,000 allowance. That replaced the older 'one of each type' rule. Keep a running total so you do not go over the limit.
tips.source: GOV.UK – Individual Savings Accounts (explained on this site's investments guide)

quiz.question: What is the ISA allowance for the 2026/27 tax year?
quiz.explain: The ISA allowance is £20,000 across all your ISAs in 2026/27. £4,000 is the Lifetime ISA annual limit (which sits inside the £20,000), and £9,000 is the Junior ISA allowance.
quiz.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

quiz.question: From 1 December 2025, what is the FSCS limit for eligible deposits, per person, per banking licence?
quiz.explain: Deposit protection rose to £120,000 on 1 December 2025. It had been £85,000. The £85,000 figure still appears in other FSCS cover, for example some investment protection if a firm fails.
quiz.checked: as at 1 December 2025 (on the site cheat sheet)

quiz.question: What is the Income Tax Personal Allowance for most people in 2026/27?
quiz.explain: The Personal Allowance is £12,570. It is reduced by £1 for every £2 of income over £100,000. £50,270 is the top of the basic-rate band for England, Wales and Northern Ireland, not the allowance.

quiz.question: What is Bank Rate, as set by the Bank of England on 5 November 2026?
quiz.explain: Bank Rate was raised to 4.00% on 5 November 2026, from 3.75%. 2% is the Bank's inflation target, not Bank Rate.

quiz.question: How much Personal Savings Allowance does a basic-rate taxpayer get in 2026/27?
quiz.explain: A basic-rate taxpayer has a £1,000 Personal Savings Allowance. It is £500 for a higher-rate taxpayer and £0 for an additional-rate taxpayer. £5,000 is the starting rate for savings, which is a separate rule and shrinks as other income rises.
quiz.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

quiz.question: If someone phones claiming to be your bank, what is the safe number to call after you hang up?
quiz.explain: 159 is the number to call your bank safely after hanging up, or use the number on your card. 7726 is for forwarding scam texts. 999 is for emergencies.

quiz.question: Section 75 credit-card protection can apply to purchases in which price range, if at least part is paid by credit card?
quiz.explain: Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act 1974 can make the card provider jointly liable for purchases over £100 and up to £30,000, where at least part is paid by credit card.

quiz.question: For most goods bought online, by phone or by post, how long do you usually have to cancel after receiving the item?
quiz.explain: You can usually cancel within 14 days of receiving the item, with no reason needed, and then have a further 14 days to return it. 30 days is the short-term right to reject faulty goods, which is a different right.
quiz.source: GOV.UK – Accepting returns and giving refunds

quiz.question: How much can you pay into a Lifetime ISA in a tax year, and does it use up ISA allowance?
options: £4,000, on top of the £20,000 ISA allowance
£4,000, which counts towards the £20,000 ISA allowance
£20,000, plus a 25% bonus on all of it
quiz.explain: The Lifetime ISA annual limit is £4,000, and it counts towards the £20,000 ISA allowance. The government bonus is 25% of what you pay in (up to £1,000 a year). £9,000 is the Junior ISA allowance.
quiz.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12–17 October 2026)

quiz.question: When does the normal minimum pension age rise from 55 to 57?
quiz.explain: The normal minimum pension age is 55, rising to 57 on 6 April 2028. Some people have a protected pension age. This is not the same as State Pension age.

quiz.question: What is the full new State Pension, per week, in 2026/27?
quiz.explain: The full new State Pension is £241.30 a week in 2026/27, about £12,548 a year. You need a complete National Insurance record to get the full amount.
quiz.source: GOV.UK – The new State Pension: what you'll get
quiz.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

quiz.question: What is the current minimum workplace pension contribution, including the employer's share?
options: 3% of all earnings, all from you
5% of salary, with 1% from the employer
8% of qualifying earnings, with at least 3% from the employer
10% of qualifying earnings, all from the employer
quiz.explain: The minimum is 8% of qualifying earnings (£6,240 to £50,270) in total, and at least 3% must come from the employer.
quiz.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

quiz.question: What is the Capital Gains Tax annual exempt amount in 2026/27?
quiz.explain: The annual exempt amount is £3,000. £500 is the dividend allowance. The much higher £12,300 figure is from an earlier tax year and is no longer in force.
quiz.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

quiz.question: What is the dividend allowance in 2026/27?
quiz.explain: The dividend allowance is £500 in 2026/27. Dividends above that are taxed at 10.75%, 35.75% or 39.35%, depending on your Income Tax band. Dividends in an ISA are not taxed.
quiz.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

quiz.question: How long is a Current Account Switch Service switch designed to take?
quiz.explain: Where both banks are in the service, the switch is designed to complete in 7 working days, with payments redirected and a refund guarantee if it goes wrong.

quiz.question: What rule of thumb does MoneyHelper give for an emergency fund?
options: One week's spending in cash under the mattress
Three to six months' essential outgoings in an instant-access account
A year of salary in a fixed bond
Whatever is left after investing first
quiz.explain: MoneyHelper describes three to six months' essential outgoings in an instant-access account as a rule of thumb. It is guidance, not a product, and the right amount depends on your circumstances.
quiz.source: MoneyHelper – Emergency savings: how much is enough?

quiz.question: A representative APR must be available to at least what share of people who are accepted?
quiz.explain: The advertised representative APR must be available to at least 51% of people accepted. Up to 49% can be offered a higher rate.

quiz.question: How long is the short-term right to reject faulty goods and ask for a refund?
quiz.explain: The short-term right to reject lasts 30 days. Other rights can last longer, but 30 days is the short-term refund window for a fault. 14 days is the usual cooling-off period for distance sales, which is about changing your mind, not faults.

quiz.question: What is the normal minimum age for accessing a private pension today, before 6 April 2028?
quiz.explain: It is 55 today, and it rises to 57 on 6 April 2028. 66 is in the region of State Pension age for many people, which is a different thing and depends on your date of birth.

quiz.question: If an authorised investment firm fails (after 1 April 2019), what is the FSCS investment protection limit per person, per firm?
options: £85,000, and it also covers the investment falling in value
£85,000, but it does not cover a fall in value
quiz.explain: Investment protection is up to £85,000 per person, per firm if the firm fails. It does not cover the investment simply falling in value. The £120,000 limit is for eligible deposits, not this type of investment cover.

myths.claim: UK bank deposits are still protected by the FSCS up to £85,000 per person, per banking licence.
myths.explain: That was the old limit. Eligible deposits have been protected up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence since 1 December 2025. The £85,000 figure still appears in some other FSCS cover, such as investment protection if a firm fails.
myths.checked: as at 1 December 2025 (on the site cheat sheet)

myths.claim: You can only pay into one ISA of each type in a tax year.
myths.explain: That used to be the rule. Since 6 April 2024 you can pay into more than one ISA of the same type in a tax year, as long as you stay within the overall £20,000 allowance.

myths.claim: If your bank phones and the number looks genuine, it is safe to confirm a password or a one-time code.
myths.explain: A number can be spoofed. Hang up, wait, and call 159 or the number on the back of your card. A genuine bank will not ask you to confirm a password, PIN or one-time code in that way.

myths.claim: Third-party motor insurance is the legal minimum you need to drive on UK roads.
myths.explain: That is correct. Third-party cover is the legal minimum. It does not cover damage to your own car. This is about the legal floor, not which policy to buy.

myths.claim: If your investments fall in value, the FSCS will pay you back.
myths.explain: The FSCS can protect eligible investment business up to £85,000 per person, per firm if an authorised firm fails. It does not cover an investment simply falling in value. Your capital is at risk when you invest.

myths.claim: Everyone automatically gets a £12,570 Personal Allowance.
myths.explain: £12,570 is the standard Personal Allowance in 2026/27, but it is reduced by £1 for every £2 of income over £100,000, and it can be affected by other circumstances. Scotland also has its own bands for non-savings income.

myths.claim: For a workplace pension, the employer must contribute at least 3% of qualifying earnings towards the 8% minimum.
myths.explain: The minimum total is 8% of qualifying earnings (£6,240 to £50,270), and at least 3% must come from the employer. Your workplace scheme may ask for more than the minimum.
myths.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

myths.claim: You can take money from a workplace or personal pension at any age, like a savings account.
myths.explain: The normal minimum pension age is 55, rising to 57 on 6 April 2028 (some people have a protected pension age). Accessing a pension early is tightly limited. This is different from State Pension age.

myths.claim: For most goods bought online, by phone or by post, you can cancel within 14 days of receiving the item, without giving a reason.
myths.explain: That is the usual cooling-off period for distance sales, and you then have a further 14 days to return the item. Some items are excluded, and in-store purchases do not automatically have the same right.
myths.source: GOV.UK – Accepting returns and giving refunds

myths.claim: Chargeback on a debit card is a legal right, just like Section 75 on a credit card.
myths.explain: Chargeback is a voluntary card-scheme process, not a legal right. MoneyHelper notes you generally need to claim within 120 days. Section 75 is a legal right, and it applies to certain credit-card purchases, not debit cards in the same way.
myths.source: MoneyHelper – How you're protected when you pay by card

myths.claim: Section 75 can make a credit-card provider jointly liable for purchases over £100 and up to £30,000, if at least part is paid by credit card.
myths.explain: That is the range in Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act 1974. The purchase must cost more than £100 and no more than £30,000, and at least part must be paid by credit card.

myths.claim: If you are accepted for a loan or credit card, you will get the representative APR in the advert.
myths.explain: The representative APR only has to be available to at least 51% of people who are accepted. Up to 49% can be offered a higher rate, so always read the rate you are actually offered.

myths.claim: Bank Rate has been 4.00% since 5 November 2026.
myths.explain: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4.00% on 5 November 2026. Your own savings or mortgage rate is set by your provider and may not match Bank Rate exactly.

myths.claim: All savings interest in the UK is automatically tax-free, even outside an ISA.
myths.explain: Interest inside an ISA is tax-free. Outside an ISA, the Personal Savings Allowance is £1,000 for basic-rate taxpayers, £500 for higher-rate taxpayers and £0 for additional-rate taxpayers. A separate starting rate for savings can also apply for people with modest income.
myths.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

myths.claim: If you open several accounts with brands that share one banking licence, each account gets its own £120,000 of FSCS cover.
myths.explain: FSCS deposit protection is per person, per banking licence, not per account or per brand. If two brands share a licence, their balances are added together towards the £120,000 limit.
myths.checked: as at 1 December 2025 (on the site cheat sheet)

myths.claim: Everyone of State Pension age automatically receives the full new State Pension of £241.30 a week.
myths.explain: £241.30 a week is the full new State Pension in 2026/27, but you only get the full amount with a complete National Insurance record. Check your record and State Pension age on GOV.UK.
myths.source: GOV.UK – The new State Pension: what you'll get
myths.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12 October 2026)

myths.claim: In England and Wales, Breathing Space can give up to 60 days of legal protection from creditors, with most interest and charges frozen.
myths.explain: That is what the Debt Respite Scheme (Breathing Space) is designed to do. It is a formal process, and the official guidance or a free debt adviser is the place to check whether it applies to you.

myths.claim: If you switch current accounts, you will have to change every Direct Debit and standing order yourself, and payments can easily go missing.
myths.explain: Where both banks are in the Current Account Switch Service, the switch is designed to take 7 working days, with payments redirected and a guarantee of refunds if the switch goes wrong.

myths.claim: The £4,000 you can put in a Lifetime ISA is extra, on top of the £20,000 ISA allowance.
myths.explain: The Lifetime ISA limit of £4,000 a year counts towards the £20,000 ISA allowance, not on top of it. The 25% government bonus is added on what you pay in, up to £1,000 a year.
myths.checked: as at 2026/27 (checked on the site, 12–17 October 2026)

myths.claim: Money sitting in cash always keeps its buying power, because the number of pounds does not fall.
myths.explain: If prices rise faster than the interest you earn after tax, each pound buys less. CPI inflation was 3.5% in the year to September 2026, while the Bank of England's target is 2%. Cash is still important for emergencies and short-term needs.
myths.source: ONS – Consumer price inflation, September 2026; Bank of England inflation target
